argument_summary: The existing record supports a narrow defense of launch readiness, not a clean defense of policy compliance. Admissible evidence shows the release clears aggregate readiness by 2.2 points, had no severity-one rehearsal incidents, and will launch at 6% with rollback and monitoring. The same admissible record also shows the affected grant compliance review segment remains exposed, the rollout does not exclude that use case, and the risk acceptance draft is neither approved nor specific to that exposure. The strongest supportable position is therefore a caveated certification treatment that distinguishes operational readiness from unresolved policy conditions.
claims_about_business_cost: Escalation would delay the grant-cycle rollout path, and the record does contain evidence of limited initial exposure, rollback capability, and monitoring. That reduces operational downside relative to a full launch, but business cost and reversibility do not change the policy condition that remains unmet.
claims_about_policy: The policy text is the limiting factor. It says rollout controls and post-launch monitoring mitigate a material model-card weakness only if the affected use case is excluded or exposure is covered by reviewed risk acceptance. The admissible evidence does not show either condition. Public governance guidance on documenting limitations and monitoring supports the control posture, but it does not replace the policy predicate. On this record, the certification case can be presented only as weak and caveated rather than cleanly compliant.
concessions: Aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents support general launch readiness, not full policy compliance for the exposed weak segment.
The affected grant compliance review segment remains in scope for the initial rollout cohort.
The rollout gate is random by cohort and does not exclude the affected use case.
The risk acceptance document is only a draft, has a blank approver line, and does not address grant compliance review exposure specifically.
A 6% rollout, rollback switch, and monitoring posture do not by themselves satisfy the disclosure policy when the affected segment remains exposed.
